headline: Low-risk pair: no shared I/O or network paths are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a has no documented I/O surfaces and agent_b has clipboard/stdin/files/network all disabled, so no shared communication channel is evidenced. Without a bridge, agent_a cannot inject instructions into agent_b, and agent_b cannot feed content back into agent_a. Uncertainty is low because both profiles explicitly deny the usual channels.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added later, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's file output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Leave clipboard and stdin/stdout bridging disabled.
Do not add an MCP server between them.
Review any future file handoff for provenance markers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent has documented network egress, and agent_b cannot read files or access clipboard/stdin, while agent_a exposes no I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or outbound path shown, there is no plausible leakage route from one agent to the other or to a third party in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem read access to shared sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains network egress or API calls, reassess for exfiltration.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled.
Avoid mounting shared sensitive directories.
Confirm no hidden API connectors are enabled.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is game-playing with no documented write or network permissions, and agent_b explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because neither agent can mutate the same resource, there is no overlapping write surface and no capability conflict pathway in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given filesystem or git write access, conflict risk may emerge.
IF both agents are attached to the same mutable datastore, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep agent_b write-disabled.
Do not grant agent_a shared mutable storage.
Use separate output directories.
Add locking before any future shared-write deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a document-processing system, but its profile shows no file, stdin/stdout, or browser inputs, so it cannot currently consume agent_a output by default. agent_a also lacks documented output channels. The main residual risk is manual handoff by an operator, which is a small blast-radius pathway rather than a default cascade.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b inputs, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is configured to trust upstream text without verification, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before any handoff.
Use a checklist for copied outputs.
Add a verification step in the document pipeline.
Keep agent_a outputs clearly labeled as untrusted.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are documented as touched by either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. With no stated residency, retention, or regulated-data flow, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess between agent_a and agent_b. The other agent is not cited separately because the relevant compliance fields are empty for both.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdictional policy, compare those policies before use.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Record retention settings for both agents.
Verify jurisdictional requirements if sensitive data is added.
Reassess after any compliance-scoped change.
